Fuzzing Zephyr Apps - Struggles of Dynamic Analysis on Embedded Applications - Jayashree Srinivasan, Analog Devices

Fuzzing, a type of dynamic analysis, is a testing method to find security flaws in software during execution. It involves providing randomized inputs to the application and observing for crashes.

Embedded applications present unique fuzzing challenges. Unlike general-purpose software, they run continuously in real-time without terminating, making it hard to use traditional fuzzing approaches. They receive inputs through specialized peripherals or direct memory/register accesses that require accurate modeling. author: The Linux Foundation
description:
Open source maintainers are facing a crisis that has nothing to do with funding or community size. Since late 2024, AI-assisted contributions have caused code volume to explode, and the humans responsible for reviewing that code cannot keep up. The review bottleneck is now the single biggest threat to project quality, security, and architectural integrity.

In this exclusive interview with Swapnil Bhartiya at TFiR, Madelyn Olson, Valkey project maintainer and Principal Engineer at AWS, breaks down exactly how the Valkey project is using AI agents to absorb that surge without sacrificing correctness, security, or the long-term vision of the project. From adversarial bug-finding that uncovered an embargoed CVE to automated backporting pipelines and provenance checking against Redis license conflicts, Olson gives a practitioner-level account of what actually works.

Key Topics Covered:
- How a 30% increase in PRs translated to a 500% increase in lines of code changed, and why that ratio
title: How Valkey Uses AI Agents Without Losing Control | Madelyn Olson, AWS
